text: Let's walk one Update Set through its whole real lifecycle. You're the admin on Dev, incident routing is broken for one category, and the fix needs two changes: a corrected Business Rule and an ACL granting the new assignment group access. You scope both into one Update Set, Q3 Incident Routing Fix.

Step one: before touching anything, you create that Update Set and switch to it in the picker. That order matters -- edit first and create the Update Set after, and the edit lands in Default instead. Step two: you make both changes, captured automatically. Step three: you review the related list, confirm exactly two changes, and mark it Complete.

Step four, you export from Dev and retrieve on Test, following the required direction -- Dev to Test to Production, never skipping Test. Step five, you run Preview on Test. The Business Rule comes back clean, but the ACL flags a real collision: a teammate edited that same ACL's role requirement directly on Test, outside any Update Set.
This is exactly the scenario from the last lesson -- two people touching the same configuration independently, and Preview catching it before either version silently wins.

Step six: you don't let either side win by default. You compare both versions and realize they're not actually in conflict in substance -- your teammate adjusted a different role requirement than the one you added. The right fix is a merge: you edit the ACL on Test to include both requirements, then mark your Update Set's version resolved.

Step seven: with the Business Rule clean and the collision deliberately resolved, you commit on Test and retest with realistic data -- before this Update Set ever gets a chance to move toward Production. Next up: Chapter Eight begins, tying the whole course back to the certification exam.
